title: On Praying for rain all through July
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：pray　|　正文 348 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 pray 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1958 the tailor ① prayed for rain all through July in the rain, and every customer in the shop said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the tailor ② prays for rain all through July without complaint without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ pray for rain all through July at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ prayed for rain all through July before — a line in the order for November 1952 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Praying for rain all through July in the rain, the tailor said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the needle at the far mirror, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ pray for a safe return before dark without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Pray for a safe return before dark at once and never mention it again.

By 1965 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the order, and a new customer from the next shop ⑧ prays for a safe return before dark in the rain every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the mirror, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ prayed for rain all through July again when nobody else would.

⑩ To pray for rain all through July, my mother said in 1970, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the shop remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the shop forgets, somebody prays for rain all through July without complaint again and somebody must pray for rain all through July in the rain all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 祈祷（一般过去式 prayed for rain all through July：1958 年裁缝头一回这样做，淋着雨）
B. v. 祈祷（一般现在 prays for rain all through July：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 祈祷（不定式 to pray for rain all through July：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 祈祷（过去完成时 had prayed for rain all through July：1952 年十一月的订单簿上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 祈祷（动名词 praying for rain all through July 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 祈求（pray for a safe return before dark：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去祈求祈求天黑前平安回来）
G. v. 祈求（pray for a safe return before dark：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 祈祷（后段两处：新来的顾客照例 prays for a safe return before dark，而母亲又一次 prayed for rain all through July）

answers.why: pray 意为“祈祷”，1958 年裁缝淋着雨祈祷整个七月求一场雨，那是裁缝铺里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 prayed。
pray 意为“祈祷”，自那以后裁缝毫无怨言地把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 prays。
pray 意为“祈祷”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯祈祷整个七月求一场雨”，此处为不定式 to pray for rain all through July。
pray 意为“祈祷”，订单簿里 十一月 那行字说明早在 1965 年之前就有人祈祷过，故用过去完成时 had prayed。
pray 意为“祈祷”，裁缝说“祈祷整个七月求一场雨这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 praying for rain all through July 作主语。
pray 意为“祈求”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去祈求祈求天黑前平安回来”，should ever 之后用原形 pray for a safe return before dark。
pray 意为“祈求”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻祈求祈求天黑前平安回来（pray for a safe return before dark at once），以后再也不要提起。
pray 意为“祈祷”，新来的顾客每个星期都照例祈求祈求天黑前平安回来，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 prays。
pray 意为“祈祷”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次淋着雨祈祷整个七月求一场雨，用一般过去式 prayed 叙述。
pray 意为“祈祷”，结尾那句是母亲 1970 年的话：要祈祷整个七月求一场雨，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和裁缝铺记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 pray 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1958 the tailor prayed for rain all through July in the rain, and nobody in the shop forgot it.
Even now the tailor prays for rain all through July without complaint whenever the shop asks.
Praying for rain all through July in the rain, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever pray for a safe return before dark without complaint, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new customer from the next shop prays for a safe return before dark in the rain every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother prayed for rain all through July again, and the shop remembered that half.
